messages.content:
You are an expert synthetic chemist planning experiments to maximise reaction yield.
Each experiment chooses one option for every variable listed. You will see the results
of experiments already run. Choose the next batch to find the highest-yield conditions
in as few experiments as possible. Use chemical knowledge (ligand and base effects,
substrate reactivity, solvent effects) and the observed results. Balance exploiting
good regions with testing informative new combinations. Never repeat an experiment.
Return JSON only.

Pd-catalysed direct C-H arylation of an imidazole to form 5-(2-fluorophenyl)-1-methyl-1H-imidazole-4-carbonitrile (Shields et al., Nature 2021, reaction 3); choose the base, ligand, solvent, concentration and temperature.

Variables and options:
base:
B1: cesium pivalate [SMILES O=C([O-])C(C)(C)C.[Cs+]]
B2: potassium pivalate [SMILES O=C([O-])C(C)(C)C.[K+]]
B3: cesium acetate [SMILES O=C([O-])C.[Cs+]]
B4: potassium acetate [SMILES O=C([O-])C.[K+]]

ligand:
L1: PPhtBu2 [SMILES CC(C)(C)P(C1=CC=CC=C1)C(C)(C)C]
L2: BrettPhos [SMILES CC(C)C1=CC(C(C)C)=C(C(C(C)C)=C1)C2=C(P(C3CCCCC3)C4CCCCC4)C(OC)=CC=C2OC]
L3: X-Phos [SMILES CC(C1=C(C2=CC=CC=C2P(C3CCCCC3)C4CCCCC4)C(C(C)C)=CC(C(C)C)=C1)C]
L4: GorlosPhos HBF4 [SMILES CC(OC1=C(P(C2CCCCC2)C3CCCCC3)C(OC(C)C)=CC=C1)C]
L5: tBPh-CPhos [SMILES CN(C)C1=CC=CC(N(C)C)=C1C2=CC=CC=C2P(C(C)(C)C)C3=CC=CC=C3]
L6: PPhMe2 [SMILES CP(C)C1=CC=CC=C1]
L7: PPh2Me [SMILES CP(C1=CC=CC=C1)C2=CC=CC=C2]
L8: CgMe-PPh [SMILES C[C@]1(O2)O[C@](C[C@]2(C)P3C4=CC=CC=C4)(C)O[C@]3(C)C1]
L9: JackiePhos [SMILES FC(F)(F)C1=CC(P(C2=C(C3=C(C(C)C)C=C(C(C)C)C=C3C(C)C)C(OC)=CC=C2OC)C4=CC(C(F)(F)F)=CC(C(F)(F)F)=C4)=CC(C(F)(F)F)=C1]
L10: PPh3 [SMILES P(C1=CC=CC=C1)(C2=CC=CC=C2)C3=CC=CC=C3]
L11: P(fur)3 [SMILES P(C1=CC=CO1)(C2=CC=CO2)C3=CC=CO3]
L12: PCy3 HBF4 [SMILES P(C1CCCCC1)(C2CCCCC2)C3CCCCC3]

solvent:
S1: N,N-dimethylacetamide [SMILES CC(N(C)C)=O]
S2: p-xylene [SMILES CC1=CC=C(C)C=C1]
S3: butyronitrile [SMILES CCCC#N]
S4: n-butyl acetate [SMILES CCCCOC(C)=O]

concentration:
C1: 0.057 M
C2: 0.1 M
C3: 0.153 M

temperature:
T1: 90 °C
T2: 105 °C
T3: 120 °C

Experiments so far (best first):
B1 | L3 | S3 | C3 | T3 -> 78.4%
B1 | L3 | S3 | C2 | T1 -> 69.1%
B1 | L3 | S3 | C2 | T2 -> 68.5%
B1 | L3 | S3 | C2 | T3 -> 59.8%
B3 | L4 | S3 | C1 | T3 -> 49.1%
B1 | L4 | S3 | C2 | T3 -> 48.1%
B1 | L3 | S3 | C1 | T3 -> 31.5%
B2 | L5 | S3 | C1 | T3 -> 6.2%
B1 | L1 | S4 | C1 | T3 -> 0.0%
B2 | L7 | S2 | C1 | T1 -> 0.0%

Propose exactly 20 NEW experiments not listed above. Return JSON:
{"picks": [{"base": "<label>", "ligand": "<label>", "solvent": "<label>", "concentration": "<label>", "temperature": "<label>", "reason": "<one sentence>"}]}

picks.reason: This tests whether the high yield at the strongest concentration is retained below 120 °C, where the C2 results suggest temperature effects may be nonmonotonic.
This checks whether the concentrated XPhos condition can achieve high yield at the lowest temperature.
This isolates the potassium-versus-cesium pivalate effect under the current best ligand, solvent, concentration, and temperature.
This tests whether cesium acetate can match cesium pivalate in the high-performing XPhos condition.
This compares potassium acetate with the leading cesium pivalate condition while holding the other variables fixed.
BrettPhos is a bulky electron-rich biaryl phosphine and is a promising alternative to XPhos for this coupling.
This tests whether the smaller, electron-rich PPhMe2 ligand can outperform the bulky phosphine in the optimized reaction environment.
This evaluates a diphenylmethyl phosphine as a distinct ligand class under the leading conditions.
This probes a structurally distinct chiral phosphine for activity in the established high-yielding base-solvent combination.
JackiePhos is a bulky electron-rich biaryl phosphine, making it a useful alternative to the successful XPhos ligand.
This provides a triphenylphosphine benchmark under the best known conditions despite its lower steric demand.
This tests whether the electron-rich tri-furyl phosphine is compatible with the successful pivalate and nitrile-solvent conditions.
This evaluates a strongly donating trialkylphosphine alternative under the current best reaction conditions.
Earlier L4 results were moderate at lower concentrations, so this checks whether the higher concentration improves its performance.
This tests whether polar aprotic DMAc improves the reaction relative to the leading butyronitrile solvent.
This assesses whether nonpolar p-xylene can support the high-yielding XPhos condition.
This tests butyl acetate as an alternative solvent while retaining the leading base and ligand.
